tool_use_result.originalFile:
# Robustness of the kernel-derived communication patterns to
#  (1) RaCInG parameters / model choices (sensitivity scenarios S1-S4),
#  (2) cohort resampling (patient bootstrap) and outlier samples,
#  (3) the patient phenotype clustering.
# Monte Carlo (simulation) robustness is assessed separately in 03_robustness_montecarlo.R.
source("/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/78d8073c6b/work/results/scripts/common.R")
suppressMessages(library(cluster))
set.seed(2)

OUT <- file.path(RES, "robustness")
dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE)
TOPN <- 10

load_scenario <- function(dir, inputs = file.path(dir, "inputs")) {
  kl <- load_kernel(inputs, file.path(dir, "kernel_raw/result.rds"), file.path(dir, "kernel_norm/result.rds"))
  D <- read_feat(file.path(dir, "kernel_raw/result_features_D.csv"))
  E <- edge_fraction(kl)
  i <- which(kl$ct == colnames(kl$C)[1]); j <- which(kl$ct == colnames(kl$C)[2])
  chk <- unname(D[, paste0("Dir_", kl$ct[i], "_", kl$ct[j])]) - unname(E[i, j, ] + E[j, i, ])
  stopifnot(max(abs(chk)) < 1e-10)   # Cmatrix CSV order matches the kernel's cell types
  list(D_raw = D,
       D_norm = read_feat(file.path(dir, "kernel_norm/result_features_D.csv")),
       W_raw = wedges(kl, FALSE), W_norm = wedges(kl, TRUE))
}

scen_dirs <- c(
  main = file.path(RES, "main"),
  S1_funLR_prod = file.path(RES, "sensitivity/S1_funLR_prod"),
  S2_exprThr5 = file.path(RES, "sensitivity/S2_exprThr5"),
  S3_exprThr20 = file.path(RES, "sensitivity/S3_exprThr20"),
  S4_immuneOnly = file.path(RES, "sensitivity/S4_immuneOnly")
)
sc <- list()
sc$main <- {
  m <- file.path(RES, "main")
  kl <- load_kernel(file.path(m, "01_inputs"), file.path(m, "02_kernel_raw/result.rds"), file.path(m, "03_kernel_norm/result.rds"))
  list(D_raw = read_feat(file.path(m, "02_kernel_raw/result_features_D.csv")),
       D_norm = read_feat(file.path(m, "03_kernel_norm/result_features_D.csv")),
       W_raw = wedges(kl, FALSE), W_norm = wedges(kl, TRUE))
}
for (s in names(scen_dirs)[-1]) sc[[s]] <- load_scenario(scen_dirs[[s]])

is_share <- function(ft) grepl("_raw$", ft)
cohort_stat <- function(X, ft) if (is_share(ft)) apply(X / rowSums(X), 2, median) else apply(X, 2, median)

## ---- (1) Sensitivity scenarios vs main ----
sens <- list()
for (s in names(sc)[-1]) for (ft in c("D_raw", "D_norm", "W_raw", "W_norm")) {
  A <- sc$main[[ft]]; B <- sc[[s]][[ft]]
  feats <- intersect(colnames(A), colnames(B))
  if (s == "S4_immuneOnly") feats <- feats[!grepl("Cancer", feats)]
  A <- A[, feats]; B <- B[rownames(A), feats]
  if (is_share(ft)) { A <- A / rowSums(A); B <- B / rowSums(B) }   # shares within the compared set
  a <- apply(A, 2, median); b <- apply(B, 2, median)
  topA <- names(sort(a, decreasing = TRUE))[1:TOPN]; topB <- names(sort(b, decreasing = TRUE))[1:TOPN]
  per_feat <- sapply(feats, function(f) suppressWarnings(cor(A[, f], B[, f], method = "spearman")))
  sens[[length(sens) + 1]] <- data.table(
    scenario = s, feature_type = ft, n_features_compared = length(feats),
    cohort_rank_spearman = cor(a, b, method = "spearman"),
    top10_overlap = length(intersect(topA, topB)),
    main_top3_ranks_in_scenario = paste(match(topA[1:3], names(sort(b, decreasing = TRUE))), collapse = ","),
    median_per_feature_patient_spearman = median(per_feat, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_features_patient_spearman_gt_0.8 = 100 * mean(per_feat > 0.8, na.rm = TRUE))
}
sens <- rbindlist(sens)
fwrite(sens, file.path(OUT, "sensitivity_scenarios_vs_main.csv"))

## ---- (2) Patient bootstrap and outlier exclusion (main analysis) ----
boot_tab <- list()
for (ft in c("D_raw", "D_norm", "W_raw", "W_norm")) {
  X <- sc$main[[ft]]
  if (!is_share(ft)) X <- X[, colMeans(X > 0) > 0.5]       # enrichment only where defined in most patients
  full <- cohort_stat(X, ft)
  top <- names(sort(full, decreasing = TRUE))[1:TOPN]
  B <- replicate(1000, {
    st <- cohort_stat(X[sample(nrow(X), replace = TRUE), ], ft)
    r <- rank(-st, ties.method = "min")
    r[top]
  })
  rownames(B) <- top
  boot_tab[[ft]] <- data.table(feature_type = ft, feature = top, full_rank = 1:TOPN,
                               boot_median_rank = apply(B, 1, median),
                               boot_rank_95CI = apply(B, 1, function(r) paste(quantile(r, c(.025, .975)), collapse = "-")),
                               pct_boot_in_top10 = 100 * rowMeans(B <= TOPN),
                               pct_boot_same_rank = 100 * rowMeans(B == seq_len(TOPN)))
}
boot_tab <- rbindlist(boot_tab)
fwrite(boot_tab, file.path(OUT, "bootstrap_top10_stability.csv"))

outliers <- c("Gide_8_PD1_PRE",      # low library complexity (~4.6k genes > 1 TPM)
              "Gide_36_PD1_PRE",     # no tumor fraction, 65% neutrophils
              "Gide_33_ipiPD1_PRE")  # extreme raw triangle counts (rare NK)
loo <- rbindlist(lapply(c("D_raw", "D_norm", "W_raw", "W_norm"), function(ft) {
  X <- sc$main[[ft]]
  if (!is_share(ft)) X <- X[, colMeans(X > 0) > 0.5]
  a <- cohort_stat(X, ft); b <- cohort_stat(X[!rownames(X) %in% outliers, ], ft)
  data.table(feature_type = ft, cohort_rank_spearman = cor(a, b, method = "spearman"),
             top10_overlap = length(intersect(names(sort(a, decreasing = TRUE))[1:TOPN],
                                              names(sort(b, decreasing = TRUE))[1:TOPN])))
}))
fwrite(loo, file.path(OUT, "outlier_exclusion_vs_main.csv"))

## ---- (3) Phenotype agreement across scenarios ----
ari <- function(a, b) {
  t <- table(a, b); n <- sum(t); s <- function(x) sum(choose(x, 2))
  e <- s(rowSums(t)) * s(colSums(t)) / choose(n, 2)
  (s(t) - e) / ((s(rowSums(t)) + s(colSums(t))) / 2 - e)
}
assign_main <- fread(file.path(RES, "main/05_patterns/patient_phenotypes_assignment.csv"))
k <- length(unique(assign_main$cluster))
pheno <- rbindlist(lapply(names(sc)[-1], function(s) {
  D <- sc[[s]]$D_raw[assign_main$patient, ]
  cl <- cutree(hclust(dist(sqrt(D / rowSums(D))), "ward.D2"), k)
  data.table(scenario = s, ARI_vs_main = ari(assign_main$cluster, cl),
             pct_same_assignment = 100 * max(mean(cl == assign_main$cluster), mean(cl == 3 - assign_main$cluster)))
}))
fwrite(pheno, file.path(OUT, "phenotype_agreement_scenarios.csv"))

## ---- Figure ----
p <- ggplot(sens, aes(x = feature_type, y = scenario, fill = cohort_rank_spearman)) +
  geom_tile() + geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("rho=%.2f\ntop10=%d/10\npt-rho=%.2f", cohort_rank_spearman,
                                              top10_overlap, median_per_feature_patient_spearman)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue", limits = c(0, 1)) + theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Sensitivity of kernel patterns vs main analysis",
       subtitle = "rho: cohort-level ranking; top10: overlap of top-10; pt-rho: median per-feature patient-level Spearman")
save_plot(p, file.path(OUT, "fig_sensitivity_scenarios.pdf"), 10, 6)

cat("\n== Sensitivity scenarios ==\n"); print(sens, digits = 3)
cat("\n== Bootstrap top-10 stability ==\n"); print(boot_tab, digits = 3)
cat("\n== Outlier exclusion ==\n"); print(loo, digits = 3)
cat("\n== Phenotype agreement ==\n"); print(pheno, digits = 3)

input.content:
# Robustness of the communication patterns to the stochastic network realization:
# RaCInG Monte Carlo (20 random graphs/patient, 10,000 cells, mean degree 20)
# vs the deterministic kernel (main analysis inputs).
source("/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/78d8073c6b/work/results/scripts/common.R")
set.seed(3)

M <- file.path(RES, "main")
OUT <- file.path(RES, "robustness/montecarlo")
dir.create(OUT, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
N_GRAPHS <- 20
TOPN <- 10

## ---- Monte Carlo output, harmonized to direction-free keys ----
mc <- readRDS(file.path(M, "04_montecarlo/result.rds"))$output
mc_csv_rows <- read.csv(file.path(M, "04_montecarlo/Results/Gide_MC_D.csv"), check.names = FALSE)[, 1]
kl <- load_kernel(file.path(M, "01_inputs"), file.path(M, "02_kernel_raw/result.rds"), file.path(M, "03_kernel_norm/result.rds"))
patients <- kl$patients

parts <- function(x) strsplit(sub("^(Dir|W|TT|CT|GSCC)_", "", x), "_")
key_of <- function(type, x) {
  p <- parts(x)
  vapply(p, function(v) switch(type,
    D = paste(sort(v), collapse = "-"),
    W = paste0(paste(sort(v[c(1, 3)]), collapse = "-"), " via ", v[2]),
    TT = , CT = paste(sort(v), collapse = "-"),
    GSCC = v[1]), "")
}
# Aggregate the columns of X (patients x features) that share a key.
by_key <- function(X, keys) {
  u <- unique(keys)
  out <- sapply(u, function(k) rowSums(X[, keys == k, drop = FALSE]))
  if (is.null(dim(out))) out <- matrix(out, nrow = nrow(X))
  dimnames(out) <- list(rownames(X), u)
  out
}
mc_mat <- function(type, what) {
  X <- as.matrix(mc[[type]][[what]])
  if (is.null(rownames(X)) || all(rownames(X) == as.character(seq_len(nrow(X))))) rownames(X) <- mc_csv_rows
  colnames(X) <- short(colnames(X))
  X[patients, , drop = FALSE]
}

types <- c("D", "W", "TT", "CT", "GSCC")
MCm <- list(); MCs <- list(); KER <- list()
feat <- readRDS(file.path(M, "05_patterns/kernel_features_corrected.rds"))$raw
for (t in types) {
  m <- mc_mat(t, "mean"); s <- mc_mat(t, "sd")
  stopifnot(identical(colnames(m), colnames(s)))
  keys <- key_of(t, colnames(m))
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(keys))           # MC features are already direction-free
  colnames(m) <- colnames(s) <- keys
  MCm[[t]] <- m; MCs[[t]] <- s
  kf <- feat[[t]]
  if (t == "GSCC") kf <- kf[, colnames(kf) != "GSCC_total"] / kf[, "GSCC_total"]   # composition of the GSCC
  KER[[t]] <- by_key(kf, key_of(t, colnames(kf)))
}

## ---- (1) Simulation noise: CV across the 20 random networks ----
noise <- rbindlist(lapply(types, function(t) {
  m <- MCm[[t]]; s <- MCs[[t]]
  share <- m / rowSums(m)
  cv <- s / m
  big <- share >= 0.01                          # features carrying >= 1% of the patient's motifs
  data.table(type = t,
             median_CV_all_nonzero = median(cv[m > 0]),
             median_CV_features_ge1pct = median(cv[big & m > 0]),
             pct_ge1pct_features_CV_lt_10pct = 100 * mean(cv[big & m > 0] < 0.10),
             median_CV_of_20graph_mean = median(cv[m > 0]) / sqrt(N_GRAPHS))
}))
fwrite(noise, file.path(OUT, "simulation_noise_CV.csv"))

## ---- (2) Reliability: between-patient vs simulation variance (per feature) ----
reli <- rbindlist(lapply(types, function(t) {
  m <- MCm[[t]]; s <- MCs[[t]]
  keep <- colMeans(m > 0) > 0.5
  vb <- apply(m[, keep, drop = FALSE], 2, var)
  vw <- colMeans(s[, keep, drop = FALSE]^2)
  data.table(type = t, feature = colnames(m)[keep],
             ICC_single_network = vb / (vb + vw),
             ICC_20graph_mean = vb / (vb + vw / N_GRAPHS))
}))
fwrite(reli, file.path(OUT, "reliability_per_feature.csv"))
reli_sum <- reli[, .(n_features = .N, median_ICC_single_network = median(ICC_single_network),
                     pct_ICC_single_gt_0.9 = 100 * mean(ICC_single_network > 0.9),
                     median_ICC_20graph_mean = median(ICC_20graph_mean)), by = type]
fwrite(reli_sum, file.path(OUT, "reliability_summary.csv"))

## ---- (3) Per-patient stability of the dominant interaction in one random network ----
# Normal approximation of a single realization: N(mean, sd) per feature.
dom <- rbindlist(lapply(c("D", "W"), function(t) {
  m <- MCm[[t]]; s <- MCs[[t]]
  rbindlist(lapply(patients, function(p) {
    mu <- m[p, ]; sg <- s[p, ]
    o <- order(-mu); top1 <- names(mu)[o[1]]; top3 <- names(mu)[o[1:3]]
    draws <- matrix(rnorm(1000 * length(mu), mu, sg), nrow = 1000, byrow = TRUE)
    colnames(draws) <- names(mu)
    w1 <- colnames(draws)[max.col(draws, "first")]
    t3 <- apply(draws, 1, function(d) names(d)[order(-d)[1:3]])
    data.table(type = t, patient = p, top1 = top1,
               pct_networks_same_top1 = 100 * mean(w1 == top1),
               pct_networks_same_top3_set = 100 * mean(apply(t3, 2, function(x) setequal(x, top3))))
  }))
}))
fwrite(dom, file.path(OUT, "patient_dominant_interaction_stability.csv"))
dom_sum <- dom[, .(median_pct_same_top1 = median(pct_networks_same_top1),
                   pct_patients_top1_ge95 = 100 * mean(pct_networks_same_top1 >= 95),
                   median_pct_same_top3_set = median(pct_networks_same_top3_set)), by = type]

## ---- (4) Kernel vs Monte Carlo ----
agree <- rbindlist(lapply(types, function(t) {
  A <- KER[[t]]; B <- MCm[[t]]
  com <- intersect(colnames(A), colnames(B))
  A <- A[, com]; B <- B[, com]
  per_patient <- sapply(patients, function(p) cor(A[p, ], B[p, ], method = "spearman"))
  keep <- colMeans(B > 0) > 0.5
  per_feature <- sapply(com[keep], function(f) suppressWarnings(cor(A[, f], B[, f], method = "spearman")))
  a <- apply(A / rowSums(A), 2, median); b <- apply(B / rowSums(B), 2, median)
  ta <- names(sort(a, decreasing = TRUE))[1:min(TOPN, length(a))]
  tb <- names(sort(b, decreasing = TRUE))[1:min(TOPN, length(b))]
  data.table(type = t, n_features = length(com),
             median_within_patient_spearman = median(per_patient),
             min_within_patient_spearman = min(per_patient),
             median_across_patient_spearman = median(per_feature, na.rm = TRUE),
             cohort_ranking_spearman = cor(a, b, method = "spearman"),
             top10_overlap = length(intersect(ta, tb)),
             kernel_top3 = paste(ta[1:3], collapse = "; "), montecarlo_top3 = paste(tb[1:3], collapse = "; "))
}))
fwrite(agree, file.path(OUT, "kernel_vs_montecarlo_agreement.csv"))

# Cohort summaries from Monte Carlo, side by side with the kernel ranks.
for (t in types) {
  A <- KER[[t]]; B <- MCm[[t]]
  com <- intersect(colnames(A), colnames(B))
  ks <- apply(A[, com] / rowSums(A[, com]), 2, median)
  ms <- share_summary(B[, com])
  ms[, kernel_median_share := ks[feature]]
  ms[, kernel_rank := rank(-kernel_median_share, ties.method = "min")]
  ms[, mc_rank := seq_len(.N)]
  ms[, median_CV := apply(MCs[[t]][, feature, drop = FALSE] / MCm[[t]][, feature, drop = FALSE], 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)]
  fwrite(ms, file.path(OUT, sprintf("cohort_summary_montecarlo_%s.csv", t)))
}

## ---- (5) Patient axis reproduced by Monte Carlo ----
pca <- readRDS(file.path(M, "05_patterns/patient_axis_pca.rds"))
pc1 <- fread(file.path(M, "05_patterns/patient_axis_PC1_scores.csv"))
kD <- feat$D; kkeys <- key_of("D", colnames(kD))
Bm <- MCm$D[, kkeys]; colnames(Bm) <- colnames(kD)
Hmc <- sqrt(Bm / rowSums(Bm))[pc1$patient, rownames(pca$rotation)]
axis_rho <- abs(cor(predict(pca, Hmc)[, 1], pc1$neutro_to_mono_axis_PC1, method = "spearman"))

## ---- Figures ----
lab_t <- function(t) c(D = "Direct", W = "Wedge", TT = "Trust triangle", CT = "Cycle triangle", GSCC = "GSCC")[t]
pd <- rbindlist(lapply(c("D", "W", "TT", "CT"), function(t) {
  A <- KER[[t]]; B <- MCm[[t]]; com <- intersect(colnames(A), colnames(B))
  data.table(type = lab_t(t), kernel = apply(A[, com] / rowSums(A[, com]), 2, median),
             mc = apply(B[, com] / rowSums(B[, com]), 2, median), feature = com)
}))
p1 <- ggplot(pd, aes(kernel * 100, mc * 100)) + geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(alpha = .5, size = 1) + facet_wrap(~type, scales = "free") + theme_bw() +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = pd[, .SD[order(-mc)][1:3], by = type], aes(label = feature), size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "Kernel: median % of patient's motifs", y = "Monte Carlo: median % of patient's motifs",
       title = "Kernel vs Monte Carlo cohort-level patterns")
p2 <- ggplot(reli, aes(x = lab_t(type), y = ICC_single_network)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.size = .5) +
  theme_bw() + labs(x = NULL, y = "ICC (single random network)",
                    title = "Between-patient vs simulation variance")
save_plot(p1, file.path(OUT, "fig_kernel_vs_montecarlo.pdf"), 10, 8)
save_plot(p2, file.path(OUT, "fig_reliability_ICC.pdf"), 7, 5)

cat("\n== Simulation noise ==\n"); print(noise, digits = 3)
cat("\n== Reliability ==\n"); print(reli_sum, digits = 3)
cat("\n== Dominant interaction stability (single network) ==\n"); print(dom_sum, digits = 3)
cat("\n== Kernel vs Monte Carlo ==\n"); print(agree, digits = 3)
cat("\nPatient axis (PC1) kernel vs Monte Carlo Spearman:", round(axis_rho, 3), "\n")
fwrite(data.table(metric = "patient_axis_PC1_spearman_kernel_vs_MC", value = axis_rho), file.path(OUT, "patient_axis_kernel_vs_mc.csv"))
for (t in c("D", "W", "TT", "CT", "GSCC")) {
  cat("\n== Monte Carlo top", t, "==\n")
  print(fread(file.path(OUT, sprintf("cohort_summary_montecarlo_%s.csv", t)))[1:8,
        .(feature, median_share = round(100 * median_share, 2), pct_top5 = round(pct_patients_top5),
          kernel_rank, median_CV = round(median_CV, 3))])
}

# Robustness of the communication patterns to the stochastic network realization:
# RaCInG Monte Carlo (20 random graphs/patient, 10,000 cells, mean degree 20)
# vs the deterministic kernel (main analysis inputs).
source("/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/78d8073c6b/work/results/scripts/common.R")
set.seed(3)

M <- file.path(RES, "main")
OUT <- file.path(RES, "robustness/montecarlo")
dir.create(OUT, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
N_GRAPHS <- 20
TOPN <- 10

## ---- Monte Carlo output, harmonized to direction-free keys ----
mc <- readRDS(file.path(M, "04_montecarlo/result.rds"))$output
mc_csv_rows <- read.csv(file.path(M, "04_montecarlo/Results/Gide_MC_D.csv"), check.names = FALSE)[, 1]
kl <- load_kernel(file.path(M, "01_inputs"), file.path(M, "02_kernel_raw/result.rds"), file.path(M, "03_kernel_norm/result.rds"))
patients <- kl$patients

parts <- function(x) strsplit(sub("^(Dir|W|TT|CT|GSCC)_", "", x), "_")
key_of <- function(type, x) {
  p <- parts(x)
  vapply(p, function(v) switch(type,
    D = paste(sort(v), collapse = "-"),
    W = paste0(paste(sort(v[c(1, 3)]), collapse = "-"), " via ", v[2]),
    TT = , CT = paste(sort(v), collapse = "-"),
    GSCC = v[1]), "")
}
# Aggregate the columns of X (patients x features) that share a key.
by_key <- function(X, keys) {
  u <- unique(keys)
  out <- sapply(u, function(k) rowSums(X[, keys == k, drop = FALSE]))
  if (is.null(dim(out))) out <- matrix(out, nrow = nrow(X))
  dimnames(out) <- list(rownames(X), u)
  out
}
mc_mat <- function(type, what) {
  X <- as.matrix(mc[[type]][[what]])
  if (is.null(rownames(X)) || all(rownames(X) == as.character(seq_len(nrow(X))))) rownames(X) <- mc_csv_rows
  colnames(X) <- short(colnames(X))
  X[patients, , drop = FALSE]
}

types <- c("D", "W", "TT", "CT", "GSCC")
MCm <- list(); MCs <- list(); KER <- list()
feat <- readRDS(file.path(M, "05_patterns/kernel_features_corrected.rds"))$raw
for (t in types) {
  m <- mc_mat(t, "mean"); s <- mc_mat(t, "sd")
  stopifnot(identical(colnames(m), colnames(s)))
  keys <- key_of(t, colnames(m))
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(keys))           # MC features are already direction-free
  colnames(m) <- colnames(s) <- keys
  MCm[[t]] <- m; MCs[[t]] <- s
  kf <- feat[[t]]
  if (t == "GSCC") kf <- kf[, colnames(kf) != "GSCC_total"] / kf[, "GSCC_total"]   # composition of the GSCC
  KER[[t]] <- by_key(kf, key_of(t, colnames(kf)))
}

## ---- (1) Simulation noise: CV across the 20 random networks ----
noise <- rbindlist(lapply(types, function(t) {
  m <- MCm[[t]]; s <- MCs[[t]]
  share <- m / rowSums(m)
  cv <- s / m
  big <- share >= 0.01                          # features carrying >= 1% of the patient's motifs
  data.table(type = t,
             median_CV_all_nonzero = median(cv[m > 0]),
             median_CV_features_ge1pct = median(cv[big & m > 0]),
             pct_ge1pct_features_CV_lt_10pct = 100 * mean(cv[big & m > 0] < 0.10),
             median_CV_of_20graph_mean = median(cv[m > 0]) / sqrt(N_GRAPHS))
}))
fwrite(noise, file.path(OUT, "simulation_noise_CV.csv"))

## ---- (2) Reliability: between-patient vs simulation variance (per feature) ----
reli <- rbindlist(lapply(types, function(t) {
  m <- MCm[[t]]; s <- MCs[[t]]
  keep <- colMeans(m > 0) > 0.5
  vb <- apply(m[, keep, drop = FALSE], 2, var)
  vw <- colMeans(s[, keep, drop = FALSE]^2)
  data.table(type = t, feature = colnames(m)[keep],
             ICC_single_network = vb / (vb + vw),
             ICC_20graph_mean = vb / (vb + vw / N_GRAPHS))
}))
fwrite(reli, file.path(OUT, "reliability_per_feature.csv"))
reli_sum <- reli[, .(n_features = .N, median_ICC_single_network = median(ICC_single_network),
                     pct_ICC_single_gt_0.9 = 100 * mean(ICC_single_network > 0.9),
                     median_ICC_20graph_mean = median(ICC_20graph_mean)), by = type]
fwrite(reli_sum, file.path(OUT, "reliability_summary.csv"))

## ---- (3) Per-patient stability of the dominant interaction in one random network ----
# Normal approximation of a single realization: N(mean, sd) per feature.
dom <- rbindlist(lapply(c("D", "W"), function(t) {
  m <- MCm[[t]]; s <- MCs[[t]]
  rbindlist(lapply(patients, function(p) {
    mu <- m[p, ]; sg <- s[p, ]
    o <- order(-mu); top1 <- names(mu)[o[1]]; top3 <- names(mu)[o[1:3]]
    draws <- matrix(rnorm(1000 * length(mu), mu, sg), nrow = 1000, byrow = TRUE)
    colnames(draws) <- names(mu)
    w1 <- colnames(draws)[max.col(draws, "first")]
    t3 <- apply(draws, 1, function(d) names(d)[order(-d)[1:3]])
    data.table(type = t, patient = p, top1 = top1,
               pct_networks_same_top1 = 100 * mean(w1 == top1),
               pct_networks_same_top3_set = 100 * mean(apply(t3, 2, function(x) setequal(x, top3))))
  }))
}))
fwrite(dom, file.path(OUT, "patient_dominant_interaction_stability.csv"))
dom_sum <- dom[, .(median_pct_same_top1 = median(pct_networks_same_top1),
                   pct_patients_top1_ge95 = 100 * mean(pct_networks_same_top1 >= 95),
                   median_pct_same_top3_set = median(pct_networks_same_top3_set)), by = type]

## ---- (4) Kernel vs Monte Carlo ----
agree <- rbindlist(lapply(types, function(t) {
  A <- KER[[t]]; B <- MCm[[t]]
  com <- intersect(colnames(A), colnames(B))
  A <- A[, com]; B <- B[, com]
  per_patient <- sapply(patients, function(p) cor(A[p, ], B[p, ], method = "spearman"))
  keep <- colMeans(B > 0) > 0.5
  per_feature <- sapply(com[keep], function(f) suppressWarnings(cor(A[, f], B[, f], method = "spearman")))
  a <- apply(A / rowSums(A), 2, median); b <- apply(B / rowSums(B), 2, median)
  ta <- names(sort(a, decreasing = TRUE))[1:min(TOPN, length(a))]
  tb <- names(sort(b, decreasing = TRUE))[1:min(TOPN, length(b))]
  data.table(type = t, n_features = length(com),
             median_within_patient_spearman = median(per_patient),
             min_within_patient_spearman = min(per_patient),
             median_across_patient_spearman = median(per_feature, na.rm = TRUE),
             cohort_ranking_spearman = cor(a, b, method = "spearman"),
             top10_overlap = length(intersect(ta, tb)),
             kernel_top3 = paste(ta[1:3], collapse = "; "), montecarlo_top3 = paste(tb[1:3], collapse = "; "))
}))
fwrite(agree, file.path(OUT, "kernel_vs_montecarlo_agreement.csv"))

# Cohort summaries from Monte Carlo, side by side with the kernel ranks.
for (t in types) {
  A <- KER[[t]]; B <- MCm[[t]]
  com <- intersect(colnames(A), colnames(B))
  ks <- apply(A[, com] / rowSums(A[, com]), 2, median)
  ms <- share_summary(B[, com])
  ms[, kernel_median_share := ks[feature]]
  ms[, kernel_rank := rank(-kernel_median_share, ties.method = "min")]
  ms[, mc_rank := seq_len(.N)]
  ms[, median_CV := apply(MCs[[t]][, feature, drop = FALSE] / MCm[[t]][, feature, drop = FALSE], 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)]
  fwrite(ms, file.path(OUT, sprintf("cohort_summary_montecarlo_%s.csv", t)))
}

## ---- (5) Patient axis reproduced by Monte Carlo ----
pca <- readRDS(file.path(M, "05_patterns/patient_axis_pca.rds"))
pc1 <- fread(file.path(M, "05_patterns/patient_axis_PC1_scores.csv"))
kD <- feat$D; kkeys <- key_of("D", colnames(kD))
Bm <- MCm$D[, kkeys]; colnames(Bm) <- colnames(kD)
Hmc <- sqrt(Bm / rowSums(Bm))[pc1$patient, rownames(pca$rotation)]
axis_rho <- abs(cor(predict(pca, Hmc)[, 1], pc1$neutro_to_mono_axis_PC1, method = "spearman"))

## ---- Figures ----
lab_t <- function(t) c(D = "Direct", W = "Wedge", TT = "Trust triangle", CT = "Cycle triangle", GSCC = "GSCC")[t]
pd <- rbindlist(lapply(c("D", "W", "TT", "CT"), function(t) {
  A <- KER[[t]]; B <- MCm[[t]]; com <- intersect(colnames(A), colnames(B))
  data.table(type = lab_t(t), kernel = apply(A[, com] / rowSums(A[, com]), 2, median),
             mc = apply(B[, com] / rowSums(B[, com]), 2, median), feature = com)
}))
p1 <- ggplot(pd, aes(kernel * 100, mc * 100)) + geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(alpha = .5, size = 1) + facet_wrap(~type, scales = "free") + theme_bw() +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = pd[, .SD[order(-mc)][1:3], by = type], aes(label = feature), size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "Kernel: median % of patient's motifs", y = "Monte Carlo: median % of patient's motifs",
       title = "Kernel vs Monte Carlo cohort-level patterns")
p2 <- ggplot(reli, aes(x = lab_t(type), y = ICC_single_network)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.size = .5) +
  theme_bw() + labs(x = NULL, y = "ICC (single random network)",
                    title = "Between-patient vs simulation variance")
save_plot(p1, file.path(OUT, "fig_kernel_vs_montecarlo.pdf"), 10, 8)
save_plot(p2, file.path(OUT, "fig_reliability_ICC.pdf"), 7, 5)

cat("\n== Simulation noise ==\n"); print(noise, digits = 3)
cat("\n== Reliability ==\n"); print(reli_sum, digits = 3)
cat("\n== Dominant interaction stability (single network) ==\n"); print(dom_sum, digits = 3)
cat("\n== Kernel vs Monte Carlo ==\n"); print(agree, digits = 3)
cat("\nPatient axis (PC1) kernel vs Monte Carlo Spearman:", round(axis_rho, 3), "\n")
fwrite(data.table(metric = "patient_axis_PC1_spearman_kernel_vs_MC", value = axis_rho), file.path(OUT, "patient_axis_kernel_vs_mc.csv"))
for (t in c("D", "W", "TT", "CT", "GSCC")) {
  cat("\n== Monte Carlo top", t, "==\n")
  print(fread(file.path(OUT, sprintf("cohort_summary_montecarlo_%s.csv", t)))[1:8,
        .(feature, median_share = round(100 * median_share, 2), pct_top5 = round(pct_patients_top5),
          kernel_rank, median_CV = round(median_CV, 3))])
}

---
name: racing-kernel-pitfalls
description: RaCInG 0.3.0 kernel issues found on Gide cohort — wedge enumeration bug, tiny-abundance blowup, sample-name and tumor-fraction gotchas
metadata:
  type: project
---

Found 2026-10-24 while running RaCInG (R pkg 0.3.0, via RaCInG-server MCP) on data/Gide_log2TPM.txt:

1. **Kernel wedge enumeration bug**: `calculateWedges` (kernel path) builds grid with k >= j (hub index) instead of k >= i, so hubs early in alphabetical order get 121 features (with duplicated leaf pairs) and late ones (NK) only 11; 220 of 726 true wedges missing. Monte Carlo W output is correct (hub = middle name, 66 leaf pairs per hub). Workaround: recompute wedges from the kernel arrays (`wedges()` in results/scripts/common.R) — matches MC at Spearman 0.999.
2. **Tiny abundances blow up raw W/TT**: kernel weights are L/colSums(L*C); abundances like 1e-16 (quanTIseq float residue) or <0.1% make raw W/TT explode (up to 1e11). Fix used: floor fractions <0.001 to 0 and renormalize. Raw TT still scales ~C^-3 for rare types — summarize with ranks/medians.
3. Sample IDs starting with digits break `prepare_racing_inputs` (make.names adds "X") → prefix IDs (used "Gide_").
4. RaCInG's internal quanTIseq drops the "uncharacterized" (tumor) fraction → immune-only network; pass deconv_csv with it renamed `Quantiseq_TIL10_Cancer` to include tumor.

**Why:** these silently distort results. **How to apply:** check for them whenever running RaCInG kernel features; see [[machine-memory-limits]].

---
name: machine-memory-limits
description: Workstation has 20 cores but only ~5.5 GB free RAM; RaCInG Monte Carlo OOMs above ~6 workers and parallel MCP R calls get killed
metadata:
  type: project
---

Observed 2026-10-24: 20 cores, 15 GB RAM with ~10 GB used by other things, swap full → ~5.5 GB available.

- RaCInG Monte Carlo (10,000 cells, degree 20, all motif types) costs ~63 s per graph per patient; each PSOCK worker uses 0.5–0.9 GB. 12 workers OOM-crashed; 6 workers is the safe max (73 patients × 20 graphs ≈ 4.3 h). Ran it directly via Rscript in background (results/scripts/run_montecarlo.R) rather than the blocking MCP tool.
- While MC runs, MCP calls that load the RaCInG input rds (explain_lr_contributions, prepare_racing_inputs) can be OOM-killed (exit -9) — especially if issued in parallel. Run them sequentially or after MC.
- `pkill -f <pattern>` can kill the calling shell if the pattern appears in its own command line; kill by PID instead.

**How to apply:** size parallel jobs to available memory, not core count. Related: [[racing-kernel-pitfalls]].

---
name: racing-kernel-pitfalls
description: "RaCInG 0.3.0 kernel issues found on Gide cohort — wedge enumeration bug, tiny-abundance blowup, sample-name and tumor-fraction gotchas"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 26081f4a-1397-4517-9ff6-bef5d565f88a
  modified: 2026-10-24T10:48:34.827Z
---

Found 2026-10-24 while running RaCInG (R pkg 0.3.0, via RaCInG-server MCP) on data/Gide_log2TPM.txt:

1. **Kernel wedge enumeration bug**: `calculateWedges` (kernel path) builds grid with k >= j (hub index) instead of k >= i, so hubs early in alphabetical order get 121 features (with duplicated leaf pairs) and late ones (NK) only 11; 220 of 726 true wedges missing. Monte Carlo W output is correct (hub = middle name, 66 leaf pairs per hub). Workaround: recompute wedges from the kernel arrays (`wedges()` in results/scripts/common.R) — matches MC at Spearman 0.999.
2. **Tiny abundances blow up raw W/TT**: kernel weights are L/colSums(L*C); abundances like 1e-16 (quanTIseq float residue) or <0.1% make raw W/TT explode (up to 1e11). Fix used: floor fractions <0.001 to 0 and renormalize. Raw TT still scales ~C^-3 for rare types — summarize with ranks/medians.
3. Sample IDs starting with digits break `prepare_racing_inputs` (make.names adds "X") → prefix IDs (used "Gide_").
4. RaCInG's internal quanTIseq drops the "uncharacterized" (tumor) fraction → immune-only network; pass deconv_csv with it renamed `Quantiseq_TIL10_Cancer` to include tumor.

**Why:** these silently distort results. **How to apply:** check for them whenever running RaCInG kernel features; see [[machine-memory-limits]].

# Export existing main-run RaCInG results (results/main) to results/standard/.
# Conversion only: no method is rerun, no value is recomputed.
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(jsonlite))

R  <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/78d8073c6b/work/results"
M  <- file.path(R, "main")
O  <- file.path(R, "standard")
dir.create(O, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

inp <- readRDS(file.path(M, "01_inputs/result.rds"))
ct  <- inp$celltypes

# RaCInG sample IDs carry a "Gide_" prefix (digits-first IDs break make.names); map back
idmap <- read.csv(file.path(R, "inputs/sample_id_map.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
to_orig <- function(ids) {
  out <- idmap$original_id[match(ids, idmap$racing_id)]
  stopifnot(!anyNA(out))
  out
}

# composition.csv -- Cmatrix
C <- inp$Cmatrix
stopifnot(identical(colnames(C), ct))
write.csv(data.frame(patient = to_orig(rownames(C)), C, check.names = FALSE),
          file.path(O, "composition.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ligands.csv / receptors.csv -- binary cell type x gene matrices, rows in celltypes order.
# Gene symbols taken from the named copies RaCInG wrote (Results/*_Gide_main.csv), which keep
# the original symbols (e.g. HLA-DOB) instead of the make.names form in the rds (HLA.DOB).
long_assign <- function(m, gene_col) {
  f <- as.matrix(read.csv(file.path(M, sprintf("01_inputs/Results/%s_Gide_main.csv", m)),
                          row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
  f <- f[ct, , drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(max(abs(f - inp[[m]])) == 0, identical(make.names(colnames(f)), colnames(inp[[m]])))
  idx <- which(f == 1, arr.ind = TRUE)
  idx <- idx[order(idx[, "row"], idx[, "col"]), , drop = FALSE]
  d <- data.frame(cell_type = rownames(f)[idx[, "row"]], gene = colnames(f)[idx[, "col"]])
  names(d)[2] <- gene_col
  d
}
write.csv(long_assign("Lmatrix", "ligand"),   file.path(O, "ligands.csv"),   row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(long_assign("Rmatrix", "receptor"), file.path(O, "receptors.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# direct_interactions.csv -- kernel D features, norm = FALSE, remove_direction = TRUE (as returned)
D <- as.matrix(readRDS(file.path(M, "02_kernel_raw/result.rds"))$features$D)
parse_pair <- function(nm) {
  s <- sub("^Dir_", "", nm)
  for (a in ct) {
    if (startsWith(s, paste0(a, "_"))) {
      b <- substring(s, nchar(a) + 2)
      if (b %in% ct) return(paste(a, "-", b))
    }
  }
  stop("cannot parse ", nm)
}
new_names <- vapply(colnames(D), parse_pair, character(1))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(new_names), length(new_names) == length(ct) * (length(ct) + 1) / 2)
colnames(D) <- new_names
write.csv(data.frame(patient = to_orig(rownames(D)), D, check.names = FALSE),
          file.path(O, "direct_interactions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# info.json
write_json(list(deconvolution_methods = "quanTIseq (TIL10 signature)",
                cibersortx = FALSE,
                deconvolution_source = "computed inside RaCInG",
                input_scale = "linear TPM"),
           file.path(O, "info.json"), auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)

cat("written:", list.files(O), "\n")

I exported all five items from the main run (`results/main/01_inputs` and `results/main/02_kernel_raw`). Nothing was skipped, recomputed or changed; the files are copies in the new format. The script is `results/scripts/export_standard.R`.

**What each file holds**
- **`composition.csv`**: 73 patients × 11 cell types, from the prepared input's Cmatrix. Cell-type names are as RaCInG has them (e.g. `Quantiseq_TIL10_CD8.cells`), and each row sums to 1.
- **`ligands.csv`** (1,577 rows) and **`receptors.csv`** (1,621 rows): every cell type–gene pair marked 1 in Lmatrix or Rmatrix. These match the RDS exactly.
- **`direct_interactions.csv`**: 73 patients × 66 cell-type pairs, the kernel's direct features as RaCInG returned them (not normalised, direction removed). 66 is every unordered pair of the 11 cell types, self-pairs included. Only the column names changed, from `Dir_A_B` to `A - B`.
- **Patient names**: RaCInG ran on IDs with a `Gide_` prefix, because IDs starting with a digit break its input preparation. I mapped them back to the original names in `data/Gide_log2TPM.txt` using `results/inputs/sample_id_map.csv`.

**Points to keep in mind when comparing**
- **Ligand and receptor names:** inside RaCInG's RDS, gene symbols were altered by R's name cleaning (`HLA.DOB`). I used the original symbols (`HLA-DOB`) from the copies RaCInG wrote to disk, after checking that the two sets of matrices agree.
- **`deconvolution_source` is a judgement call.** I chose "computed inside RaCInG". The abundances came from RaCInG's own quanTIseq run in an earlier preparation step (`results/01_racing_inputs`), and were then changed before being passed back in via `deconv_csv`:
  - The tumour fraction was kept as `Quantiseq_TIL10_Cancer`, because RaCInG's built-in quanTIseq leaves it out.
  - Fractions below 0.001 were set to 0 and the rest rescaled to sum to 1, because tiny values make the kernel scores blow up.

  If you count that as supplying my own matrix, "computed by me before RaCInG" would also fit.
- **Input scale:** RaCInG received linear TPM (`already_normalized = TRUE`). That file (`results/inputs/Gide_TPM_linear.csv`) was converted back from the log2 TPM input. Its per-sample totals are 41k–730k, not about 1e6, so the TPM is not re-normalised over the genes kept.
- **Not exported:** the sensitivity runs and the separate normalised kernel run, since they are not the main result.

Files written to `results/standard/`: composition.csv, ligands.csv, receptors.csv, direct_interactions.csv, info.json

content.text:
**1. Input data transformation**

- `data/Gide_log2TPM.txt` held values from 0 to 14.0 and was non-integer and non-negative, which fits log2(TPM+1). I converted it to linear TPM (2^x − 1) for all RaCInG steps, because both the internal deconvolution and the `expr_threshold` comparison expect linear TPM.
- The back-transformed per-sample totals were about 41k–730k, not 1e6. I assumed this was because only about 19k genes are present, and I did **not** renormalize to 1e6.
- I prefixed sample IDs with `Gide_` because names starting with a digit broke the name matching (see 4).
- No log-scale steps were run, so the log2 values were never used directly.

**2. Methods run and skipped**

- **Run:**
  - `prepare_racing_inputs`: its internal quanTIseq run, then supplied compositions afterwards.
  - `run_racing_kernel`, both raw (`norm=FALSE`) and normalized (`norm=TRUE`), for D, W, TT and GSCC.
  - `run_racing_montecarlo`: a single-patient pilot through the MCP tool. The full 73-patient run used RaCInG's `compute_racing_montecarlo` directly in a background Rscript, because the MCP call blocks and would take hours.
  - `explain_lr_contributions` for Cancer–Cancer, Cancer–Mono and Cancer–Neutro.
  - My own R scripts: cohort summaries, wedge recomputation, Ward clustering with silhouette and bootstrap, PCA axis, sensitivity, bootstrap and outlier analyses.
- **Skipped or incomplete:**
  - Other deconvolution methods: I used only quanTIseq, RaCInG's default, and did no robustness check across deconvolution methods.
  - Signed networks: kept the default `signed=FALSE`.
  - `explain_lr_contributions` for Cancer–CD8 and for the Cancer–Mono–Cancer wedge: these were OOM-killed and never rerun.
  - `03_robustness_montecarlo.R`: written but **never executed**.
  - I did not use the Riaz file, and did no survival or ML analysis.

**3. Non-default parameters**

- **Main run:**
  - `already_normalized=TRUE`, since the input was linear TPM.
  - `deconv_csv`: a custom quanTIseq composition with the "uncharacterized" fraction renamed `Cancer`, so tumor cells are part of the network.
  - That composition had fractions below 0.001 set to 0 and was renormalized. This was my preprocessing choice to stop raw W/TT values from exploding; it is not a RaCInG parameter.
- **Sensitivity runs:**
  - `fun_lr=prod` (default `min`).
  - `expr_threshold=5` and `expr_threshold=20` (default 10).
  - An immune-only composition.
- **Monte Carlo:**
  - `Ngraphs=20` (default 100), for compute time.
  - `ncores=6` (default 1); 12 workers ran out of memory.
  - Pilots used 20 and 5 graphs.
- `norm` was set both ways, to get raw magnitude and enrichment.

**4. Problems and how I handled them**

- **Sample-name mismatch error:** RaCInG added an "X" to names starting with digits. I renamed samples with a `Gide_` prefix and saved an ID map.
- **Tumor cells missing:** the internal quanTIseq run dropped the tumor/other fraction, so the network was immune-only. I supplied my own composition that includes it.
- **Exploding raw values:** raw TT values reached about 1e11, caused by abundances near zero (for example 1e-16) in the denominator. I applied the 0.001 floor; some remaining TT outliers come from rare cell types, so I summarize with medians and ranks.
- **Suspected RaCInG wedge bug:** the kernel's wedge enumeration gives uneven numbers of features per hub cell type, with 220 of 726 wedges missing and some duplicated. I found this by reading the code. I recomputed wedges from the kernel arrays using the same formula.
- **Monte Carlo crashes from memory:**
  - 12 workers crashed. I relaunched with 6 workers.
  - I stopped the second run deliberately after finding the tiny-abundance problem, and relaunched it on the floored inputs.
  - Orphaned workers were killed by PID; `pkill` also killed my own shell twice (exit 144).
- **Lost connection on the threshold-5 input run (S2):** the output files existed, and I validated `result.rds` before using it.
- **OOM-killed LR explanations** while Monte Carlo was running: two were not retried, as noted in 2.
- **My final wait command was killed (exit 137).** I never confirmed whether the Monte Carlo run finished.

**5. Checks before trusting results**

- Checked the expression scale.
- Confirmed composition rows sum to 1.
- Reproduced RaCInG's D values from the kernel by hand.
- My wedges match RaCInG's to within 1e-14 on the 506 wedges both enumerations share.
- Determined the Monte Carlo wedge hub position by matching the pilot to the kernel (Spearman 0.999).
- Ran 4 sensitivity scenarios: cohort rankings had Spearman 0.91–0.998, and the top feature was unchanged in every scenario.
- Bootstrapped patients 1000 times to test top-10 stability.
- Excluded 3 outlier samples: ranking Spearman stayed at or above 0.98.
- Checked the patient axis (PC1) across scenarios and 500 bootstraps: Spearman at or above 0.996.

**6. Limits and cautions**

- **Monte Carlo robustness is not done:** the run's completion is unknown and its analysis was never run, so robustness to random network realizations is unassessed.
- **The "Cancer" node is not purely tumor:** it is quanTIseq's uncharacterized fraction, which includes stroma and other unmodeled cells.
- **CD4 and DC sit at a median abundance of 0**, so they are effectively absent; that is a deconvolution limitation.
- **Patient clusters are weak:**
  - The k=2 silhouette is 0.30.
  - Cluster assignment collapsed under `fun_LR=prod` (ARI 0.10).
  - Use the continuous neutrophil-to-monocyte axis instead of the clusters.
- **Normalized and immune-only features are less stable**, with a patient-level ρ as low as 0.65–0.71 in the immune-only scenario.
- **The 0.001 abundance floor and the wedge fix are my own choices,** not RaCInG defaults.
- **Response associations were not significant** (p=0.13 and 0.30) and are exploratory only.
- **No final report or README was written.** `results/` still holds superseded or temporary runs that are not part of the final results: `01_racing_inputs`, `02_racing_inputs_with_tumor`, `03_kernel`, `04_kernel_raw` and the `tmp_mc_pilot*` folders.

# Export existing main-analysis results (no recomputation) to results/standard/.
suppressMessages(library(jsonlite))
RES <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/78d8073c6b/work/results"
OUT <- file.path(RES, "standard")
dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE)

idmap <- read.csv(file.path(RES, "inputs/sample_id_map.csv"))
orig <- setNames(idmap$original_id, idmap$racing_id)
inp <- readRDS(file.path(RES, "main/01_inputs/result.rds"))
ct <- inp$celltypes

# composition.csv: Cmatrix as used by RaCInG
C <- inp$Cmatrix
stopifnot(identical(colnames(C), ct), all(rownames(C) %in% names(orig)))
write.csv(data.frame(patient = orig[rownames(C)], C, check.names = FALSE),
          file.path(OUT, "composition.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ligands.csv / receptors.csv: nonzero entries of Lmatrix / Rmatrix
long <- function(X, names2, col) {
  idx <- which(X != 0, arr.ind = TRUE)
  d <- data.frame(cell_type = ct[idx[, 1]], x = names2[idx[, 2]])
  names(d)[2] <- col
  d[order(d$cell_type, d[[col]]), ]
}
stopifnot(nrow(inp$Lmatrix) == length(ct), ncol(inp$Lmatrix) == length(inp$ligands),
          nrow(inp$Rmatrix) == length(ct), ncol(inp$Rmatrix) == length(inp$receptors))
write.csv(long(inp$Lmatrix, inp$ligands, "ligand"), file.path(OUT, "ligands.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(long(inp$Rmatrix, inp$receptors, "receptor"), file.path(OUT, "receptors.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# direct_interactions.csv: raw kernel D features (remove_direction = TRUE)
D <- read.csv(file.path(RES, "main/02_kernel_raw/result_features_D.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
newnames <- character(0)

The names match exactly. The earlier failure came from how my quick check read the header, not from the export.

I exported the main analysis: quanTIseq composition including the tumor fraction, with the 0.001 abundance floor, `fun_LR=min`, threshold 10 TPM, and the raw kernel. Patient names are the original IDs, without the `Gide_` prefix I added for RaCInG. Nothing was recomputed. The export script is `results/scripts/04_export_standard.R`.

- **`composition.csv`:** the Cmatrix as RaCInG used it, 73 patients × 11 cell types.
- **`ligands.csv` / `receptors.csv`:** every cell-type/gene pair with a nonzero entry in the Lmatrix or Rmatrix (1,577 and 1,621 rows).
- **`direct_interactions.csv`:** RaCInG's own direction-removed D features from the raw kernel, renamed to `A - B`. RaCInG dropped no pairs, so all 66 unordered pairs are present.
- **`info.json`, "deconvolution_source":** I chose "computed by me before RaCInG", but the history is mixed. quanTIseq first ran inside my first `prepare_racing_inputs` call. I then took that output, relabelled its "uncharacterized" fraction as `Cancer`, applied the floor, and passed it to the main run through `deconv_csv`.

Nothing was skipped; all five requested items existed.

Files written to `results/standard/`: composition.csv, ligands.csv, receptors.csv, direct_interactions.csv, info.json
